championTitleNoWins: {champion} won the {year} title without winning a race, banking podiums every weekend while faster rivals threw it away.
Not a single victory all year, yet {champion_last} is champion — consistency outlasted the cars that beat {champion_last} for pace.
{champion} took {year} on points, not wins: no race fell to {champion_last}, but no rival matched the run of podiums.
The fastest cars kept faltering, and {champion_last} was there to collect every time — a championship built without a win.
{champion_last} never stood on the top step in {year} and still took the title, the steadiest hand while quicker drivers came undone.
championWinStreak: {champion} reeled off win after win without interruption, and that unbroken run carried the {year} title.
A long streak of victories, one after another, was the spine of {champion_last}'s championship.
{champion_last} went weekend after weekend unbeaten, and the run of wins settled {year} early.
Once {champion} started winning, the wins did not stop — a sustained streak that decided the title.
The {year} championship turned on a run of consecutive {champion_last} victories that no rival could break.
championComebackMerit: {champion} was off the lead early, then strung together a second-half run of wins to chase {early_leader_last} down for the {year} title.
Behind {early_leader_last} at the midpoint, {champion_last} answered with victory after victory and overhauled that early lead by {gap} {gap_pts}.
{champion} started {year} adrift, then won the championship the hard way — a late surge of wins that caught {early_leader_last}.
The early lead was {early_leader_last}'s; the title is {champion_last}'s, taken back on pace with a closing run of wins.
{champion_last} trailed, then won when it mattered, race after race, to overhaul {early_leader_last} and claim {year}.
championComebackHanded: {champion} came from behind in {year}, though it was {early_leader_last}'s retirements, not {champion_last}'s pace, that surrendered the lead.
The deficit closed without {champion_last} having to take it — {early_leader_last} kept retiring, and the title slipped {champion}'s way.
{champion_last} ended up champion after starting behind, but {early_leader_last} handed the early lead over with a run of DNFs rather than being beaten outright.
A comeback in the standings, yes — driven by {early_leader_last} dropping points to retirements more than by anything {champion} did on track.
{champion} inherited the lead late, the gap erased not by {champion_last} winning races but by {early_leader_last} failing to finish.
championThreeWay: Three drivers carried the title fight deep into {year}, and {champion} was the one who came through it.
A three-way scrap stayed live to the closing rounds; {champion_last} emerged from it as champion.
{champion} outlasted two rivals in a championship that stayed open three ways until late, taking {year} by {gap} {gap_pts}.
It was a three-cornered fight to the end, and {champion_last} held the nerve the other two could not.
Three names were in it with rounds to run — {champion} settled {year}, with {runner_up_last} the nearest of the chasers.
championDomination: {champion} won at least half the races in {year} — not a close title, a dominant one.
Wins came in numbers no rival could live with; {champion_last} dominated {year} from end to end.
{champion} took the title by sheer weight of victories, claiming half the season's races or more.
There was nothing marginal about {champion_last}'s {year}: a clear majority of weekends, a one-sided championship.
{champion} crushed the field, banking enough wins to put the {year} title beyond doubt.
championWireToWire: {champion} led the standings from the opening round to the last and was never headed across the {year} season.
Not once in {year} did {champion} surrender the championship lead — first after round one, first at the finish.
{champion_last} took the points lead at the season opener and held it every round to the title.
{champion} ran the table on the standings: top of the championship from the first round through to the last.
From the opening round, the lead was {champion_last}'s, and no rival took it back at any point in {year}.
championDecider: {champion} settled the {year} title in the closing rounds, finishing {gap} {gap_pts} clear of {runner_up_last}.

{gap} {gap_pts} decided {year} — {champion_last} held off {runner_up_last} to the last.

{champion_last} edged {runner_up_last} by {gap} {gap_pts}, the {year} championship decided in the final rounds.
championClear: {champion} took over the championship lead during the season and pulled clear, ending {year} comfortably ahead of {runner_up_last}.
Once {champion_last} hit the front of the standings, the margin only grew; {year} ended a comfortable {gap} {gap_pts} over {runner_up_last}.
{champion} did not lead from the start but, having taken the lead, won {year} going away by {gap} {gap_pts}.
{champion_last} assumed the championship lead in-season and stretched it, finishing {year} clear of {runner_up}.
After taking over at the top, {champion} controlled {year} to a comfortable {gap} {gap_pts} margin over {runner_up_last}.
